pilot.summary: Three-player pod at Tom's, me on Edgar, Alex on Sauron, Tom on blue-black. Five vampires down by turn three off three mana spent, and the whole table made Markov the problem immediately — I ate multiple wipes and a stack of counters, and rebuilt in a turn or two every time. I did not cast Edgar until I had eight mana, which is my own mistake; when he landed it was the finisher, and Olivia's Wrath into a wide haste swing got Alex to 1. Tom countered Champion of Dusk and Bloodthirsty Conqueror, I needed one more vampire, and had nothing.

Five-player pod at Oliver's, second game of the night, seat 5. Mulliganed once and kept a two-land hand out of stubbornness — I knew at the time it should have gone back. Blood Artist and Bloodthirsty Conqueror landed early and a wipe with the drain online killed eleven creatures: every opponent lost 11, I gained 11, and I was around 50 to the table's 20. Then Ryan's recurring artifact and enchantment removal picked off Anointed Procession and the rest, I ran out of steam with vampires on board and nothing in hand, and Deflecting Swat and Teferi's Protection sat uncast all game because the mana was always spent on vampires.

Three-player pod at Alex's in Orinda, game two of four, me against Alex and Stuart. "Best-case opener and it did not matter" — two lands plus Sol Ring into a Talisman, four mana on turn one, Edgar down fast, Warleader's Call and the token-enters enchantments in place — and then Edgar was the only vampire I cast all game. Got Alex to 12 commander damage before he assembled blockers and he closed later with an oversized threat; I ran out of steam on card draw again. The conversation with Alex afterwards is the part that matters: the deck changes direction from swarm typal to lords and payoffs, tokens become the dig engine, and the token-conversion axis from 25 August is withdrawn.

Five-player pod at Oliver's, game three of three, first night on the twelve-swap list. Tom's Goblin Sharpshooter pinged my tokens and that fed the card-draw creatures, so I was running my engine off his removal. I resolved a big flyer that draws cards, brought Edgar down, then pivoted to Bloodletter of Aclazotz for the doubled damage and swung lethal into Alex to take him out. Tom tutored a two-card infinite and closed before my lethal resolved — a loss with Edgar dominating the board, and one I want on record as unsatisfying in a way that losing to a better board is not.

Four-player pod at Alex's, first of two games on the night: me on Edgar, Oliver on Vito mono-black vampires, Tom on Purphoros mono-red goblin ETB, Alex on an Azorius counters deck. Strong opener — Viscera Seer turn one off a swamp for the eminence token and its sac ability used early, never missed a land drop, Elspeth out, then Edgar off Ancient Tomb on turn five — and early vampires plus Edgar swinging held momentum all game; Oliver said afterwards he was always a turn behind. I went too all-in on Tom with Elspeth exposed, she got taken down, and Tom's Purphoros ETB pings finished the job before my lethal landed, about an hour in. The two lessons I wrote down: once a planeswalker is online, keep blockers up and protect the engine before pushing tempo; and Purphoros is the natural predator for mid-range aggro, so the deck needs targeted disruption in white.

Four-player pod at Oliver's, first of two games, Tom in India: me on Edgar, Ryan on Teval, Oliver on a blue-black mill deck, Alex on his spaceships novelty deck. I ate board wipe after board wipe and rebuilt fast each time, but only into small blockers, and by turn eight, nine, ten I did not have enough cards in hand to play things. I played Vish Kal too early and did not hit Blood Artist until mid-game, so the wipes came with neither doing its job; Markov came down, I swung into a wider board with bigger +1/+1 counters, and could not convert before the next wipe. At one point I could have made a 12/12 flying lifelink with Vish Kal and Vito on board, but I went after Alex, who had indestructible creatures; we worked him to about seven, Oliver almost milled him out, and I sat there in my vampire nest — no result filed for this game, cause filed as wipe.

read.what_it_does: On v1.1.1 — one game, 006 — it built a wide vampire board with Markov out and bigger +1/+1 counters, ate board wipe after board wipe, rebuilt fast into small blockers ('stuff that keeps me alive through some combat, nothing threatening'), and could not convert before the next wipe. The death payoffs never got to run: Blood Artist was not hit until mid-game, and Vish Kal, the outlet that turns the small creatures into one huge one and gets around indestructible, went down too early (006). On v1.1.0 the same opening was the deck the table chased and combat is what threatened to close — Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubling damage into a wide swing that took Alex out (004), Edgar off Ancient Tomb on turn five holding momentum all game (005) — and every card those two games name is still in the 99. But 006 is the only game on the list I am holding, and it ran out of steam by turn eight to ten the way the V1 games did (001, 002, 003), which is my own word for it: 'the consistent theme with Edgar is it runs out of steam' (006).
read.how_it_plays: Creature-heavy and visible, with not a lot of protection, so the table wipes it: 'board wipe after board wipe' (006), the same as on V1 — multiple wipes and a stack of counters aimed at me (001), rebuild, wipe, rebuild (002). It comes back fast every time, but on 006 the rebuild was small blockers rather than a threat, and by turn eight to ten the hand was empty. Where it ended up on the current list: one moment of momentum — a 12/12 flying lifelink available off Vish Kal with Vito on board — spent on the wrong target, Alex's indestructible board, and then 'I just malaised there in my vampire nest' while Oliver nearly milled Alex out and Ryan did graveyard things (006). On v1.1.0 it ended ahead on board with lethal in sight and beaten by a clock it could not block — a tutored two-card infinite (004), Purphoros ETB pings (005). My own read after 006: it plays like a creature deck, and I want it to play like life gain / life drain, with ways to assign damage that is not combat damage.
mindful_of: Sequence Vish Kal and Blood Artist for the wipe, not before it. Vish Kal went down too early, Blood Artist was not hit until mid-game, so a run of wipes happened with neither in place and then Blood Artist died to one too (006). Both are still in the 99.

Do not swing the big lifelinker into the indestructible board. The 12/12 flying lifelink was there off Vish Kal with Vito on board, and I went after Alex, who had indestructible creatures — 'basic stuff: maybe don't go after the player with the indestructible board' (006). Same shape as V1: Alex's Nazgul kept growing and I saw it too late (001, on V1).

Running out of steam is back on the current list. 'Get out to turn eight, nine, ten and not have enough cards in hand to play things' (006). All three V1 games ended with vampires on board and nothing in hand (001, 002, 003); neither v1.1.0 game did (004, 005). diagnosis.json's verdict reads the deck as developing well and closing worse than its board deserves, on 004 and 005 — 006 is a current-list game where the hand ran dry first, and the rebuilds were blockers, not threats.

The generic 'every vampire gets +1/+1 when a creature dies' cards are not helping much — 'I need the engine that makes the deaths happen, not to sit around waiting for creatures to die' (006). I did not name which cards; the note files it as a direction for the next pass, not a swap made.

Protection stays in hand or is not there. 'Not a lot of protection' on the current list (006); on V1 Deflecting Swat and Teferi's Protection sat uncast a whole game because the mana was spent on vampires, and the reason was structural: a deck that cannot afford to hold up interaction is a deck that does not run interaction (002). Both cards are still in the 99.

Swing lethal when it is there, at the right player. Both v1.1.0 games were lost with lethal in sight — Tom closed before it resolved (004), Tom's pings got there before it landed (005) — and on 006 the momentum moment went into an indestructible board. 'Sequence and close better' is my own summary of where the tuning sits (005), and 006 did not change it.

Pushing tempo with Elspeth exposed. I went too all-in on Tom, she got taken down, and Purphoros's pings finished it (005, on v1.1.0). My lesson from that night: once a planeswalker is online, keep blockers up and protect the engine before pushing tempo. She was targeted immediately on V1 too (001) and is still in the 99.

A Purphoros-style ETB deck is the natural predator for this mid-range aggro plan and the deck has no targeted disruption for it — no blue, and nothing in white doing that job (005, on v1.1.0). The follow-up I filed was white disruption; the v1.1.1 swaps were both death payoffs, so it is still a filed follow-up.

You are the archenemy from turn three and the answers come at you first — five vampires by turn three off three mana and the whole table decided Markov was the problem (001, on V1), Oliver a turn behind all game (005), wipe after wipe (006). My own read: the correct read, and the price of the plan.

Edgar's cast is a decision, not what happens when the mana is spare. Eight mana before he came down, because 'I had not even been thinking about him' (001, on V1); turn five off Ancient Tomb is what it looks like when it goes right (005).
The refuel is what gets countered. Champion of Dusk, the draw-five that would have closed it, and Bloodthirsty Conqueror both ate counters in one game (001, on V1), and both are still in the 99.

Ryan's recurring artifact and enchantment removal picks off the doublers. Anointed Procession resolved and was gone the following turn (002, on V1); on the current list it is 'a great card, hard to get off' (006), and Ryan was at the table both times.
Mulligan discipline. One mulligan, then a two-land hand kept out of stubbornness, knowing at the time it should have gone back (002).
Tight lines get missed in the moment. I could have paid more life, faster, to pump the vampire and drawn a pile of extra cards off the death trigger (004).
Seat 5 in a five-player pod. My read is that the first-seat momentum advantage compounds with the mana deficit rather than just adding to it (002).
read.what_changed: 006 is the first game on v1.1.1, the list I am holding: v1.1.0 plus two swaps settled 2026-09-16 from the elenda-v1 branch — Elenda, the Dusk Rose for Immersturm Predator and Blade of the Bloodchief for Unbounded Potential, both death payoffs. Neither incoming card is named in 006, so the game says nothing about them either way. What 006 does say about the list is a direction change, filed in the note itself: the deck is 'super creature heavy', 'plays like a creature deck', and I want the life gain / life drain axis to be the engine, not decoration — 'ways to assign damage that is not combat damage' — while the generic +1/+1-on-death cards 'are not helping much'. What I want measured for the next pass, staying bracket 3 with no two-card infinites: life gained and life drained over a game, damage assigned through Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Vito and anything that doubles it, and a threat axis — big vampires fast with flying / lifelink / deathtouch, average creature size (006). Before that: V1 to v1.1.0 was the twelve-swap list decided after 003, swarm typal to lords and payoffs with tokens as the dig engine, and 004 and 005 on v1.1.0 did not run dry — 'the refactor really showed' (004), and after 005 the tuning had moved from 'rebuild the deck' to 'sequence and close better'. 006 says the running dry came back on the current list, from one game. Three older details are superseded and stay out of the read: 001's Olivia's Wrath finisher, 003's Warleader's Call opener and my own Purphoros on V1 all left with the twelve swaps, and the Purphoros that beat me in 005 was Tom's commander, not a card of mine.
